Lone Scout's Fantasy team list analysis: Round 26
Some big names return along with a couple of Fantasy specialists but still a couple of surprise outs to deal with.
Let’s get into the team lists for this week.
Broncos v Storm, Thursday 7.50pm at Suncorp Stadium
Broncos: After their come from behind win last week in Canberra, the Broncos have kept their side as is for the Grand Final rematch against the Storm. Payne Haas had a big game last week and owners will be hoping he backs up in this one.
Storm: For a third game running Tyran Wishart has a new position with Jahrome Hughes returning at halfback this week. Wishart instead finds himself at centre covering for Jack Howarth who has gone for surgery on an oft-injured shoulder. Jack Hetherington and Marion Seve are the new bench men.
First take: Broncos v Storm
Sea Eagles v Dragons, Friday 6.00pm at 4 Pines Park
Sea Eagles: Josh Feledy replaces the injured Tolutau Koula who suffered an ankle sprain last week. Onitoni Large joins the 19 as Manly fight to keep their season alive.
Dragons: Jacob Liddle is out with a calf injury which gives an opportunity for Damien Cook to give us one or two more great fantasy games before he departs to Castleford next season. Connor Muhleisen comes into the interchange but expect Cook to get a bulk of the minutes if not play the entire match.
First take: Sea Eagles v Dragons
Panthers v Bulldogs, Friday 8.00pm at CommBank Stadium
Panthers: Jack Cole is the surprise replacement for the suspended Jack Cogger at five-eighth with Blaize Talagi remaining on the six-man interchange. Jaxon Edgar takes the bench spot vacated by Cole.
Bulldogs: Enari Tuala is the only change to the side that got the job done against the Dragons last week. It should be noted that Matt Burton switched to right centre last week so Bronson Xerri could play on his preferred left side and expect the Bulldogs to run out in the same fashion on Friday night.
First take: Panthers v Bulldogs
Titans v Rabbitohs, Saturday 3.00pm at Cbus Super Stadium
Titans: Coach Josh Hannay has resisted making too many changes to the team that went down to the Sharks despite leading at half-time. Josh Patston comes back from his stint in the concussion protocols in a straight swap for the injured Beau Fermor. Max Feagai can be found amongst the extended reserves in the only other adjustment.
Rabbitohs: In a fantastic initiative by the Rabbitohs and the NRL, Jai Arrow will suit up for, and take part in, the opening seconds of this game against his former club, allowing him to potentially register 100 matches for Souths. The other big news comes via the bench with Latrell Mitchell coming back from injury. He will be joined by Jamie Humphreys and Adam Elliott in a big boost for the visitors as they fight to cement a top-eight spot.
First take: Titans v Rabbitohs
Roosters v Dolphins, Saturday 5.30pm at Allianz Stadium
Roosters: Having been teased for return for the past three weeks, coaches will again need to take the allocation of James Tedesco at fullback with a grain of salt. After putting up an incredible outing last round, Nat Butcher reverts to lock with Victor Radley dealing with a concussion. Lindsay Collins is the new prop while Taylor Losalu joins Cody Ramsey on the pine.

MUHLEISEN BACK IN THE NRL
Jacob Liddle's season-ending calf injury opens the door for Connor Muhleisen to make his first NRL appearance since Round 27, 2024.
Muhleisen played a starring role in the club's run to the 2025 Knock-On Effect NSW Cup Grand Final tallying a competition-best 806 tackles at 96 per cent efficiency before suffering an ACL rupture in the first half of the decider.
He made his return to the field in the club's Round 22 Knock-On Effect NSW Cup fixture this year and this week earns an opportunity on the big stage.
A native of Buxton in the Wollondilly Shire, Muhleisen grew up playing his juniors with the Thirlmere-Tahmoor Roosters before linking up with Illawarra as a teenager.
He represented the Steelers at Harold Matthews Cup and SG Ball level helping lead the side to a 2019 SG Ball Grand Final win.
He made the leap up to Jersey Flegg the following year before earning a maiden NSW Cup nod in Round 8, 2021.
A gritty No.9, Muhleisen grew into an integral member of the side before being rewarded with an NRL debut in Round 22, 2023.
COOK EAGER TO END ON HIGH
It's been an impressive ride for veteran rake Damien Cook who is on the home stretch of an illustrious, 14-year NRL career.
Cook made a long-awaited homecoming to the Dragons in 2025 having made his NRL debut for the club back in Round 6, 2013.
A Helensburgh Tigers junior, Cook would spend the 2014 and 2015 seasons with the Bulldogs before making the move to the Rabbitohs where he blossomed into one of the game’s elite No.9s over the course of nine seasons.
He made his State of Origin debut in Game I, 2018 before earning a Kangaroos debut later that year against New Zealand.
The 34-year-old now boasts a resumé including 261 NRL appearances, 17 State of Origin nods, four Kangaroos caps and a Dally M Hooker of the Year Award.

items.title: Blow for Penrith Panthers fans as unsung hero confirms he's signed with Bulldogs for 2027 - Yahoo News Australia
items.snippet: Blow for Penrith Panthers fans as unsung hero confirms he's signed with Bulldogs for 2027    Yahoo News Australia
items.body_excerpt:
Penrith Panthers fans will be sad to see Freddy Lussick depart the club after the dummy-half confirmed he is heading to the Bulldogs next NRL season. The Panthers signed Lussick from the Warriors on a one-year deal for 2026 to add depth in the No.9 position.
Lussick stepped into the starting No.9 role when Mitch Kenny fractured his leg, and didn't miss a beat to help the Panthers sit second on the ladder. Lussick has started in every game since Round 8 and has been one of the unsung stars of the team often making around 40 tackles a game.
Freddy Lussick (third from right) has confirmed he is leaving the club to join the Bulldogs next season. (Photo by Hannah Peters/Getty Images)
However, there had been reports in recent weeks that Lussick would out the door at season's end with the 25-year-old looking for a new contract. NRL 360 host (and former Bulldogs star) Braith Anasta put it to Lussick this week over whether he had signed for Canterbury next season.
Lussick confirmed he has but said he was trying to focus on the game this weekend, which will be against his new club. "Obviously I have got to put that in the back pocket, not think about that too much. Exciting for next year, but I have a job to do this week," Lussick said. "It's a good opportunity for me to head over there…I am looking forward to it."
While the move is yet to be confirmed by either club, Lussick will join a competitive Bulldogs squad and compete for the dummy-half role with Bailey Hayward next season. The Bulldogs' spine has come under plenty of criticism across the last 12 months and the departure of Reed Mahoney at No.9 also raised eyebrows considering his form for the Cowboys.
The No.9 will be hoping to lock down a role under coach Cameron Ciraldo. Although he will also be looking to leave Penrith as a premiership winner.
Freddy Lussick (pictured) appears to be on his way to the Bulldogs next season. (Photo by Jeremy Ng/Getty Images)
Penrith Panthers seeking premiership glory
The Panthers would like to send Lussick out a winner this season with Ivan Cleary's side sitting equal-top of the ladder with the Warriors and Roosters. A win this weekend against the Bulldogs will put them in a good position to finish Top 2 on the ladder.
This would mean avoiding a trip to New Zealand to play the Warriors in the first round of the NRL finals. The Panthers played the Wests Tigers in the final round of the season.
While Lussick is heading to the Bulldogs, fans will be keen to see Liam Martin re-sign. Martin has been in contract negotiations with the Panthers with his deal ending at the end of next season. But reports suggest the call has now been made to put talks on hold until after the NRL finals.

items.title: The Bulldogs embarrassed Penrith last time they met. Casey McLean wants to make amends - SMH.com.au
items.snippet: The Bulldogs embarrassed Penrith last time they met. Casey McLean wants to make amends    SMH.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
The most valuable lessons Casey McLean has learnt in his short NRL career came when he last faced Canterbury.
That was in round six, when the previously undefeated Penrith lost their first match of the season. It was a particularly sobering experience for McLean, who was sent to the sin bin and subsequently suspended for a shoulder charge on Bulldogs prop Max King, who was left with a broken jaw.
“Obviously I’m very sorry for what happened to him, but he’s been killing it since he’s come back,” McLean said.
“I had a little reflection in the sin bin. I sat in there [wondering], ‘I think this is actually the only time I’ve been sin binned’.”
McLean has also reflected on his defensive performance that night. The Bulldogs constantly targeted his left edge, where Lachlan Galvin and Jacob Preston in particular created several line breaks in a 32-16 win.
The NSW three-quarter will have a different pivot playing alongside him for Friday’s rematch – Jack Cole will wear the No.6 jersey in the absence of the suspended Jack Cogger – while Blaize Talagi, who was also exposed defensively in that initial Bulldogs clash, has been named on the bench.
Casey McLean is sin binned for a hit that broke Max King’s jaw. Getty Images
“We started the year well, but then the Bulldogs came and gave us a little punch in the face,” McLean said. “So it’s about not getting too comfortable.”
There are few deficiencies in a Panthers outfit that is the favourite to take out the title. However, the Bulldogs exposed their edge defence in that last outing and McLean views Friday’s clash at CommBank Stadium as an opportunity to get back on track before the finals.
“You’re never going to be perfect, but you’re always striving to be,” he said.
“So, getting as many reps and banking as much as we can together at training – even off the field, a bit of connection – that’s what we’re trying to build,” he said.
Casey McLean made his Origin debut this year. Getty Images
“Their right edge is exceptionally strong, so this will be a good challenge for us coming forward. On Friday, it’ll be a good challenge not just for our edge, but the whole team.”
It has been a rapid rise for McLean, who at the age of 20 has won a premiership and represented New Zealand and NSW. Last week, he signed a new contract that will keep him at the foot of the mountains until the end of 2030.
The Blacktown product had no desire to test his value on the open market, even though the PNG Chiefs are about to enter the fray with their tax-free dollars.
“Growing up playing for Penrith pretty much my whole life and growing up in the area, knowing that they wanted me around helped me a lot as well,” he said. “It’s been such a great club for so long; I didn’t really want to leave. Being able to flourish at this club will hopefully be a good stepping stone for my future.
“This club and all the coaching staff, they gave me the opportunity to be who I am today. I feel like I’m still at an age where some people would still be playing younger grades, but they gave me the opportunity and the chance to showcase not just who I am as a player, but a person. So I wanted to give back to this club and respect what they’ve done for me.”
McLean said he had gained confidence from being part of NSW’s State of Origin series victory.
“I found myself just backing what I’ve been told to do,” he said. “Obviously, led by skip Yeoy [Penrith and NSW captain Isaah Yeo] – ever since getting into that camp, a little bit of him just telling me, ‘You’re here for a reason’, and stuff like that.
“He’s been a big reason for why my form might have been as good as it was.”
While McLean has recommitted to the Panthers, teammate and older brother Jesse has agreed to terms with Friday’s opponents, Canterbury.

Lach us in: Bulldogs back Galvin to keep the dream alive
Lachlan Galvin has never lacked confidence and he'll need every bit of it if he's to outwit the game's premier playmaker and keep the Bulldogs' season alive.
Nathan Cleary is Galvin's senior by seven years and 146 NRL games, not to mention four premierships. But that won't stop the 21-year-old from taking the game up to Cleary as Canterbury look to emulate a Round 6 win over the Panthers and remain in the finals hunt.
Galvin's teammates have marvelled at his progress across the season and are backing him to stand tall on the back of two try assists, 123 run metres and a try in last week's demolition of the Dragons.
“Lachie doesn’t feel much pressure as it is,” said fullback Connor Tracey.
“He's been playing good all year and doesn’t deserve the stuff he cops.
“He’s a really exciting young kid.”
With two games remaining, the Bulldogs must beat the Panthers and Broncos, and rely on the Rabbitohs and Cowboys stumbling to keep their top-eight hopes alive.
Lachlan Galvin Try
And to make matters worse they have had to deal with an outbreak of COVID, with up to 10 players struck down in a throwback to the uncertain times of 2020 and '21.
“It was a tricky week with heaps of boys out, but the way everyone turned up with the right attitude [against the Dragons] just shows what we’ve got here,” said centre Matt Burton.
“It was a good step in the right direction. We attacked really well and it flowed great.
“We need to fine-tune a few things against Penrith. We know what side they are, you can’t be clunky against them, otherwise they’ll make you pay.”
Vintage Burto
The 32-16 win over the Panthers back in April was a triumph for Galvin with four line break assists and Enari Tuala, who broke seven tackles and ran for 180 metres.
Sadly for the Dogs they weren't able to back that up, falling to five straight losses after the Panthers upset, summing up the rollercoaster nature of their season.
Tracey is adamant the chance to test themselves against the best team of the modern era in a do-or-die match is one to embrace.
“Last few times we’ve played them it’s been pretty close,” he said.

“It’s cool playing Penrith, the benchmark of the competition for the last few years. It’s exciting to be playing them this time of year.
“It’s pretty simple for the rest of the season, win this week and win the next game as well.
“It’s exciting to play Penrith with all the stakes that are on that.”

items.title: Why Friday night shapes as the biggest challenge of Cleary’s club career
items.snippet: He conquered Origin seven weeks ago. On Friday night, the Panthers halfback faces an even greater challenge in clubland.
items.body_excerpt:
Nathan Cleary conquered the State of Origin arena just seven weeks ago. Now the Penrith halfback faces arguably the greatest challenge of his club career.
Cleary will run out in Friday night’s must-win match against Canterbury without the club’s first-choice lock, hooker or five-eighth.
Nathan Cleary will lead the under-strength Panthers into battle against Canterbury. Getty Images
The last time Cleary played without three key members of the Penrith spine was 2019, before the club embarked on its premiership era. Matt Burton, who will line up for the Bulldogs on Friday, debuted for Penrith in that game in the halves for the suspended James Maloney.
When halves partner Jarome Luai succumbed to a shoulder injury during the 2023 grand final, Cleary still had co-captain Isaah Yeo, hooker Mitch Kenny and fullback Dylan Edwards to lean on.
The Panthers are expected to welcome Kenny back from a leg and ankle injury next weekend, while there remains a slim chance Yeo could also play after suffering a pectoral injury three weeks ago.
In the meantime, Cleary will need to make it work at CommBank Stadium with back-up lock and hooker Lindsay Smith and Freddy Lussick, as well as Jack Cole, who plays just his third NRL game this season in place of suspended No.6 Jack Cogger.
Two of the finest playmakers to wear the Penrith jersey not only backed Cleary to deliver – again – but only if the pack did their part and dominated the Dogs.
“Without Mitch and Isaah and now a No.6, this is a massive challenge,” Greg Alexander said. “Nathan still has Dylan Edwards, who has had an outstanding year, at the back, but there’s a lot of pressure on him to create something.
“And while Isaah has always been that link man, Lindsay Smith is still providing Nathan with a little something, and helping him get wider.
“Cam Murray does the same thing for Cody Walker at Souths, and Victor Radley allows ‘DCE’ [Daly Cherry-Evans] and Sam Walker to get wider.
“Nat will have to touch the ball as many times as possible. Jack Cole is only playing his third game, but he can play, and if the Dogs only focus on Nat, Jack will hurt them.
“Canterbury played their best game against Penrith earlier this year. The forced errors from the get-go with their defensive pressure. But Penrith were coming off a hell of an opening five weeks where they won games against tough teams. Nat would have taken a lot of lessons away from that night. He’s always looking at ways to improve.
“Yes, with the injuries and suspension, we’re starting to get down the list, but it’s still a good list.”
Maloney said of Cleary: “There’s a lot more pressure on Nathan, but the footy is still the same. He’ll just have to wait for his opportunities when he’s on the front foot, then he can go at the defence and dictate them. But he needs his teammates to get him on to that front foot. He can’t do that himself.
“The danger when you’ve only got one recognised threat is defensive sides will load up and follow Nathan wherever he goes. Most teams will always do that to any player who has that much influence on the game.
James Maloney was Cleary’s halves partner early in his Penrith career. NRL Photos
“I’ve played in games where everywhere you go, they’ll pump numbers to you. By doing that, they leave opportunities for the players around you. It’s up to those players to call for the ball and take advantage of those opportunities.
“Nathan won’t care if they score four tries and he doesn’t have a hand in any of them because the Dogs sat on him all day.”
A win will keep Penrith’s top-two hopes alive with one round remaining, and also end the Dogs’ season.
Canterbury coach Cameron Ciraldo, who declared the playing group was free of COVID and Influenza A after the virus ripped through the club over the past fortnight, said they would look to learn from that excellent performance against Penrith in round six.
